card.name: Odd word starts in old prose
card.fires_on: Fires on a word or word-start in older, literary or historical prose, often just before a word that continues the phrase (e.g. a Latin or archaic term). Typical spots are mid-word pieces like p, exp, V, over, or small words like his, their, with.

modes.label: Partway through rarer words
modes.description: A split-off start of an uncommon or Latin word, where the rest of the word follows.

modes.label: Small words in historical narrative
modes.description: A possessive or linking word, or a plain verb, in 17th-19th century style prose.
modes.example: left to pursue<< their>> usual occupations.

card.plain: It marks scattered word-starts and small words in old-fashioned historical or literary text, with no single topic.
